item.title: [VIDEO] 2027: Obi Won’t Get Up To Six Million Votes, Won’t Win Lagos — YPP’s Agada
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Young Peoples Party (YPP) for the 2027 general election, Peter Agada, has said that a former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, will not secure up to 30 per cent of the six million votes he got in the 2023 presidential election. Agada stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . He said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, who was of the Labour Party (LP) in 2023, won in Lagos due to the support received from different groups, including members of the #EndSARS group, youths, and workers. ﻿ He, however, said Obi would not win in Lagos in the forthcoming presidential election. While assessing the administration of President Bola Tinubu, Agada said that though he supports Tinubu’s removal of the fuel subsidy, he has a problem with the President not targeting the real end users and subsidising the product. He also said that Nigeria is losing about 70 per cent of its revenue to overbloated contracts. He also described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway ₦1trn budget as overbloated, saying that he would construct one kilometre of the road for ₦750 million or ₦800 million. Asked whether he was part of the proposed coalition to unseat President Tinubu, Agada said no one had approached him. item.title: 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Responding to a question about Atiku’s belief that he is better positioned than President Bola Tinubu to govern Nigeria, Sowunmi said the former vice president should reconsider his ambition. “Well, he’s been saying that for a while, and Nigerians have been rejecting him,” he said. FILES: Segun Sowunmi on Channels Television’s Politics Today “If you have done elections the number of times Waziri (Atiku) has done, there is something he himself must consider. At what point in time does he expect younger, sharper northern people to get tired or be fatigued at running around with him?” he asked. North Presidency Calculations The PDP chieftain, who was a spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Organisation in 2023, also questioned the former vice president’s political calculations, noting that the North had already produced a president who governed for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He further questioned Atiku’s candidacy under the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark. The November 5 judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Abuja, followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, challenging the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku Abubakar is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress for the 2027 general elections. The ruling affected decisions taken by the committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The ADC group has rejected the judgment and appealed. Sowunmi, however, maintained that Atiku’s candidacy remained uncertain. “As at today, he is not on the ballot. Because you appeal a case you lost in the lower court, does that mean you are going to win it? The bottom line is that, as at today, he is not their candidate,” he said. He also accused Atiku of mishandling the dispute involving Gombe, describing his approach as an “emir complex”. “Emirs don’t beg, emirs don’t visit people, call others. Emirs sit at home, and everybody comes to meet them. Yes, you can be an emir, but you can’t be an emir if you are looking for a ticket in another man’s party,” he added. item.title: US judge tosses new visa rules for Nigerians, other foreign students, journalists
item.description: A US federal judge on Monday struck down a Trump administration policy that would impose stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the United States. District Judge Dennis Saylor, in his order dismissing the case, said the policy was “arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.” The new visa regulations had been scheduled to take effect in September but were temporarily put on hold by Saylor, a move the Trump administration has already appealed to a higher court. The judge’s ruling stems from a lawsuit contesting the visa restrictions filed against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) by a coalition of unions representing universities, teachers and journalists. In his order, Saylor focused mainly on the impact the new visa policy would have had on international students. “Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage,” the judge said. He said the policy would “prohibit foreign students from engaging in extended periods of study, such as those required for Ph.D. programs; prohibit them from obtaining joint degrees (and) prohibit them from changing their academic concentration.” Under the proposed new rules, foreigners on student visas would be admitted for a maximum of up to four years after which they would have to apply for an extension. International students were previously allowed to remain for the duration of their studies. Foreign journalists would be limited to stays of just 240 days, or around eight months, but could apply for extensions of similar duration. Until now they could stay up to five years. Chinese journalists would get just 90 days, with extensions of 90 days. The visa restrictions are part of a broader immigration crackdown by President Donald Trump that includes aggressive deportation operations as well as new restrictions on legal pathways to citizenship. The United States welcomed more than 1.1 million international students in the 2023-24 academic year, more than any other country, according to official data. AFP The post US judge tosses new visa rules for Nigerians, other foreign students, journalists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
item.description: A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence by protesters who chanted ‘Bamayi’ at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade, describing such actions as undemocratic. “I am disappointed, extremely disappointed that security is allowing that kind of joke to go on under the guise of people who are running democracy,” he said. Sowunmi argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate or campaign should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence. “I expect people who have a point of view different from that of a campaign to wait until the day of election to exercise their franchise. But to be destroying people’s posters, to be carrying sticks and running up and down, that’s for barbarians, and I don’t expect any sane leader to do that,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after President Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. item.title: Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. A statement from the Editor, Mr Eze Anaba, said his death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession. Mr Ajasa was a valued member of the Vanguard family, who made significant contributions to the growth of the company’s digital operations and online journalism. Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, Olufemi Ajasa obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009. He further honed his professional skills with a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015. He began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016. He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager. Ajasa returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death. His return marked the continuation of a relationship with the organisation that began early in his professional career. The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family. At this difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with his family. We pray that God grants them the strength and fortitude to bear this painful loss, and that the soul of our departed colleague finds eternal rest. The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in honour of the deceased will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. The post Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NNPP disowns Onu, threatens legal action over alleged impersonation
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) has disowned Prince Nweze Onu, who allegedly parades himself as the party’s Deputy National Chairman, describing him as an impostor who has no authority to speak or act on behalf of the party. The party also warned that Onu could face arrest over alleged impersonation, insisting that he had long been expelled from its fold alongside Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. The NNPP’s position was contained in a statement issued by its National Secretary, Comrade Oginni Olaposi Sunday, and made available to Vanguard in Abeokuta. He accused Onu of misrepresenting his political affiliation and attempting to create confusion about the party’s leadership. According to Oginni, Onu is not a recognised official of the NNPP and should not be regarded as its spokesperson or representative. “Prince Onu is not qualified to speak on behalf of our great party. He is, at the last count, a member of Kwankwasiya in NDC,” the National Secretary stated. Oginni further called on media organisations to exercise caution and verify the political affiliations and official positions of individuals before publishing statements attributed to them as representatives of political parties. “We are using this opportunity to call on all media houses to ensure that due diligence is done on verification of the status of individuals before publication,” he said. The party also condemned what it described as an attack on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu by Onu, dismissing his remarks as politically motivated and an attempt to attract attention from the Presidency. Oginni described Onu as an expired politician and rabble-rouser, arguing that his comments should not be taken seriously. “Onu is an expired politician and a rabble-rouser trying to get the attention of the Presidency. Nobody should take him seriously,” he said. The NNPP reiterated that Onu had no mandate to speak for the party, warning that individuals who falsely claim official positions within its leadership structure could face legal consequences. item.title: Lekki residents protest four-month power outage, demand substation
item.description: Accuse Eko Power, TCN of shifting blame; say businesses losing billions By Cynthia Alo Residents of more than 200 estates along the Orchid Road axis of Lekki, Lagos State, have staged a protest over prolonged electricity outages, accusing Eko Power Limited and the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) of shifting blame for the persistent disruption. The residents, under the aegis of the Lekki Conservation Estates Community Development Association (LECECODA), demanded the immediate restoration of electricity supply, provision of individual prepaid meters and construction of a dedicated injection substation to serve the Orchid Road corridor. They also called for a technical audit of the Maroko 33kV feeder, through which the community receives electricity, and urged the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) to investigate the quality of service being delivered to the area. The protest, which took place at the weekend, followed what the residents described as five years of engagements and unfulfilled commitments by the electricity distribution company. It also came barely a week after the Minister of Power, Mr Joseph Tegbe, reportedly assured residents of Lekki and Ajah communities of improved electricity supply. The protesters, comprising landlords, tenants and business owners, carried placards with inscriptions such as: “Orchid Road Deserves a Substation”, “Orchid Road Band B = Band Nothing”, “We Pay Premium Rates But Get Zero Reliability”, “Eko Power Failed Promise” and “Constant Power Outages Are Killing Businesses on Orchid Road.” Addressing journalists during the protest, LECECODA President, Bode Akinwande, said the community had received virtually no electricity for more than four months despite continuing to receive electricity bills running into millions of naira. Akinwande described Orchid Road as a 7.5-kilometre corridor housing approximately 200 residential estates, alongside schools, restaurants, shopping malls, supermarkets, clubs, churches and mosques. He said the community’s size and contribution to Eko Power’s revenue made the absence of a dedicated injection substation particularly concerning. He said: “For the past four months, we have received virtually no supply. In the month of October, we did not receive two hours of supply cumulatively. And unfortunately, members of this community, various estates, have received bills in millions. And this is not acceptable to us at all. “For five years, the leadership of this community has engaged directly with Eko Power, and before it, the former management known as EKEDC. Several meetings have been held, and several commitments have been made. None of them have been implemented.” The LECECODA president said the current management of Eko Power also met with community stakeholders at Orchid Hotel and made further assurances, but residents had yet to witness any significant improvement. item.title: Jackson scores as Senegal move closer to 2027 AFCON
item.description: Premier League duo Nicolas Jackson and El Hadji Malick Diouf scored on Monday as Senegal beat Sudan 4-2 to virtually clinch a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations tournament. Cameroon trounced Namibia 3-0 and Benin snatched a late 1-0 win over the Central African Republic to move close to qualification for the marquee African competition. Senegal, Cameroon and Benin have 10 points each from four matches and could all be confirmed as qualifiers on Tuesday depending on the other result in their groups. Cameroon and Senegal are former AFCON champions while the furthest Benin have progressed is the round of 16 at the 2025 tournament. Jackson came to Africa last week, having scored nine goals in all competitions for Aston Villa this season. He opened the scoring in a 4-1 home win over Sudan last Thursday. He also broke the deadlock with a fourth-minute goal away to Sudan, who hosted the match in South Sudan because of a civil war in their homeland. Defender Diouf, who moved from relegated West Ham United to Brentford during the close season, doubled the lead midway through the first half. Sudan staged a second-half comeback to draw level after 75 minutes through goals from substitute Al Gozoli Nooh and Salaheldin Adil. But a late Senegalese rally saw Pathe Mboup restore the lead, then set up Paul Mendy to score in added time. – Cameroon romp – Senegal won the final of previous edition of the AFCON 1-0 in extra time over hosts Morocco last February. But CAF declared Morocco champions because most of the Senegalese team temporarily left the field to protest a penalty, which Morocco missed when play resumed. Senegal have asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Switzerland to overturn the CAF ruling and a decision is expected this month. It took Cameroon 12 minutes to score away to Namibia through Mahamadou Nagida. Goals from Ryan Fosso and Saidou Alioum in the second half completed the victory. Benin left it late to secure maximum points with debutant Ede Oloko netting in added time. The goal condemned the Central African Republic to a fourth straight loss. Elsewhere, Zimbabwe outplayed Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare, Guinea beat Eritrea 3-1 in Cairo and a Jordan Ayew penalty earned Ghana an unimpressive 1-0 win over Somalia in Essipong. In the six matches on Monday, Zimbabwe were the only host nation to actually play at home. Central African Republic, Eritrea and Namibia do not have international-standard stadiums. A civil war that erupted in April 2023 prevents Sudan from playing in Khartoum and Somalia cannot stage AFCON qualifiers due to security concerns in the Horn of Africa. item.title: Yobe Empowerment: Why Tinubu, Wali Deserve Electorate’s Votes
item.description: In a move aimed at fostering economic independence among vulnerable populations, the All Progressives Congress (APC) launched a zonal empowerment campaign on Sunday, distributing essential items to 500 youth and women in Yobe State. The initiative, which took place in Gadaka, Fika Local Government Area, saw the distribution of 200 motorcycles, 100 tricycles, and 100 sewing machines to beneficiaries, a gesture designed to create sustainable livelihoods and improve economic well-being across the state. APC gubernatorial candidate Baba Malam Wali, who oversaw the distribution exercise, emphasized that the program represents more than temporary relief and would be extended to the two other zones of the state. “Rather than offering only temporary relief, this initiative, which is one of thousands of lifelines created by Governor Mai Mala Buni, would have generational change impacts across Yobe communities,” Wali stated. The APC flag bearer urged beneficiaries to make optimal use of the items, describing the intervention as an investment in their future and the economic development of the state. Tinubu’s Support: “The Shortest Way to Success” Wali attributed the impactful performance of Governor Buni to the support of the federal government under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s leadership. He also described support for President Tinubu as “the shortest way to success,” citing the administration’s impactful performance at both federal and state levels. “The volume of developmental projects executed by the APC-led government makes the re-election bid of President Tinubu and other party candidates an easy sell to the electorate,” the governorship hopeful noted. Wali urged Yobe residents to cast their ballots for President Tinubu and all APC candidates in the upcoming elections to guarantee continued progress and prosperity. He cautioned voters against supporting opposition candidates, warning: “You can’t follow a road that is leading you to nowhere.” The APC candidate expressed confidence in securing victory through development-oriented policies and programmes, pledging to sustain and consolidate Governor Buni’s initiatives focusing on youth development, economic empowerment, and continuity. Beneficiaries Hail Intervention Beneficiaries hailed the intervention as life-changing. Mohammed Inusa, 38, who received a pickup tricycle (Jega), described the gesture as unexpected. “I never thought that I will own a Jega at this time. item.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief As the Federal Government prepares its 2027 budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings. The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations. According to Efe Ovuakporie, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement in Abuja on Monday evening, under the initiative, “The Office is working towards establishing a coordinated system that will enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.” She added, “A major component of the programme is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to locate suitable venues. “The arrangement will also enable MDAs with under-utilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.” Ovuakporie said the initiative aligns with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions. In a related development, the Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-Eastern states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo, as part of efforts to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings. The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities. The exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending. Among the findings were under-utilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas. The inspection teams also identified opportunities to improve the utilisation of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records. item.title: Gunmen kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of the Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, Operation Rainbow, and another person in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victims were reportedly killed at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District of Bokkos Local Government Area. The community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, said both victims were members of his community. He said, “They are all members of my community. They went to Hurti village for a condolence visit and were returning to Tadai when suspected gunmen ambushed and killed them. “They were killed in broad daylight this afternoon. It is very sad and unfortunate.” Paul disclosed that one of the deceased was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow, adding that the killing had thrown the community into mourning. He said, “The commander had just graduated. We are deeply saddened by this incident, especially given the security challenges our people have continued to face.” Also confirming the incident, an award-winning Nigerian conflict reporter from Bokkos, Masara Kim, said the two men were killed in the ambush while returning from the condolence visit. The deceased Operation Rainbow commander was said to have recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos, Kim added. Efforts to obtain further details from security authorities were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Oshiomhole tackles Atiku over education privatisation, says Nigeria cannot afford policy
item.description: …challenges Atiku, Obi to clarify education policies ahead of 2027 By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Former Edo State Governor Adams Oshiomhole has taken a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar over his advocacy for the privatisation of tertiary education, declaring that Nigeria cannot afford to surrender its public education system to private interests when millions of children are still denied access to schooling. Oshiomhole argued that privatising tertiary education would further deepen inequality and undermine access to learning in a country still battling a huge out-of-school population, inadequate educational infrastructure and unequal opportunities. The former governor spoke on Monday in Abuja at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa. He questioned the rationale behind Atiku’s renewed push for private-sector control of tertiary education, recalling that the former Vice-President had pursued a privatisation agenda during his time in office. Oshiomhole also challenged Atiku and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to tell Nigerians whether they would sustain or dismantle the education policies introduced by the President Bola Tinubu administration if allowed to govern the country. He insisted that Nigerians deserved clarity on the opposition politicians’ education agenda, particularly on policies designed to expand access to tertiary education and provide financial assistance to students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Taking a further swipe at Atiku, Oshiomhole criticised what he described as the former Vice-President’s position on using public resources to enrich friends, warning that such an approach could undermine critical social investments, particularly education. He maintained that government resources were limited and that decisions on public spending must reflect national priorities rather than personal interests. “If the money he wishes to use to enrich his friends is not diverted to paying student grants, remember that resources are limited at any point in time. That is why economics is about priorities. What is given to those students will not be available to be used to assist friends,” he said. Nigeria’s education crisis remains a major national concern, with millions of children still excluded from formal schooling despite successive government interventions. A 2024 UNICEF estimate put the country’s out-of-school children population at 18.3 million, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age, although the Federal Ministry of Education has more recently cited an estimate of about 15 million. item.title: Tinubu’s education reforms reach 3m tertiary students, Alausa tells opposition
item.description: …Accuses opposition of misleading Nigerians, says government prioritising results over promises By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has challenged opposition politicians, particularly former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to familiarise themselves with Nigeria’s education laws before criticising the Federal Government’s policies, insisting that nearly three million tertiary students are benefiting from President Bola Tinubu’s reforms. Alausa, who accused the opposition of deliberately misrepresenting the administration’s interventions, said criticisms of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and other education policies were misplaced and failed to acknowledge the benefits Nigerians were already enjoying. The minister fired back at Obi on Monday during a briefing at the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council headquarters in Abuja, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s record in education ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a direct response to Obi’s criticisms, Alausa said the former presidential candidate needed to study the relevant legislation before making public statements about the government’s education financing arrangements. “What Mr Obi is saying is borne out of ignorance. He needs to read the law. This is the law of Nigeria,” the minister declared. He further accused Obi of misleading Nigerians, saying: “If Mr Obi wants to blame me and mislead the public and Nigerians, that tells you the kind of person he is.” At the centre of the disagreement is the four per cent development levy introduced under the Nigeria Tax Act, which Alausa said was designed to guarantee sustainable funding for the student loan scheme. He explained that 15 per cent of the proceeds from the levy was earmarked for NELFUND, insisting that the allocation was expressly provided for in the law and not an arbitrary government arrangement. The minister challenged Obi to examine the relevant provisions of the legislation rather than cast doubts on the funding structure of the scheme. Defending the broader education reforms, Alausa said the administration’s interventions had expanded access to tertiary education through student loans, improved infrastructure, increased funding and efforts to address the shortage of academic personnel in universities and other higher institutions. item.title: Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa
item.description: By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday. Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, while nine others were killed in a shack in Jeffsville, near the capital, Pretoria. Police spokesperson, Robert Netshiunda, said the identities of the eight victims in Sweetwaters were yet to be confirmed, although some families had approached authorities to assist. “It’s still too early to tell what the motive could have been and who could be behind the shooting because we are yet to identify the victims,” he said. In Jeffsville, six males and three females were found with gunshot wounds inside a four-room shack. Police spokesperson, Brenda Muridili, said officers were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Monday, although the shooting reportedly occurred between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Sunday. No arrests had been made as investigations continued. Gauteng Police Commissioner, Tommy Mthombeni, said the killings could be linked to a shooting in nearby Saulsville last year, which claimed 12 lives and left 13 others injured. He disclosed that one of Sunday’s victims was a person of interest in the previous attack, adding that police could not rule out retaliation. South Africa has recorded several deadly mass shootings in the past year. In September, 11 people, including a pregnant woman, were killed in an attack on a house near Durban, while another shooting at a tavern claimed 17 lives. Two separate shootings in Johannesburg in June also left 24 people dead, with police linking one to rival illegal mining gangs. Two other mass shootings in December last year claimed 21 lives. Police investigations into Sunday’s attacks are ongoing. The post Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria’s inflation rate drops to 14.06% in October
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) has said. The NBS disclosed this in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released on Monday, also showing a decline in food inflation to 19.13 per cent in October from 19.59 per cent in the preceding month. According to the report, headline inflation stood at 18.97 per cent in October 2025, indicating a 4.91 percentage-point decline in the annual rate between October 2025 and October 2026. The statistics agency, however, reported an increase in the month-on-month headline inflation rate, which rose to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.06 per cent in September. It explained that the development indicated that the average price level increased at a faster rate in October than in the preceding month. “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06%, down from 14.63% in September 2026 and stood at 18.97% in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025),” the NBS stated. The report added that the October 2026 headline inflation rate represented a 4.91 percentage-point decline compared with the corresponding period of the previous year. “On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43%, which was 0.38% higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06%). “This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026,” the agency said. item.title: INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo has disowned the author of a viral video, claiming to have recruited ad-hoc personnel for the commission and directing them to work for a particular political interest. In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Samuel Sunday, on behalf of the Resident Electoral Commissioner, the commission stated that the man was not its staff member. “INEC Edo declares that no one named Osayi Israel Omoroduwa is among its staff in Edo, and that no one has the power or access to recruit ad-hoc staff for the commission,” Sunday explained. He further explained that the recruitment of ad-hoc personnel was conducted exclusively through the online INECPRES platform, administered by INEC Headquarters. “The path to being an ad-hoc staff of INEC is by online application through the INECPRES platform and whoever has internet access can do so by themselves or support others so qualified to apply,” he added. He emphasised that staff members in its state offices could not influence the recruitment process, adding that the person named in the video had no special access to the platform. According to Sunday, successful applicants will undergo scrutiny by the commission and receive training on the conduct and ethics of elections. The INEC Spokesman described the online video as “an irresponsible and targeted attack” on the commission and its processes. He argued that the video was intended to undermine public confidence in the electoral process through misinformation. He, however, reaffirmed the commitment of the commission to conducting credible elections and urged the public to disregard what it described as “falsehood contained in the video”. (NAN) The post INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: We blocked channels used to siphon Abia funds — Otti
item.description: Governor attributes poor roads, dirty environment to alleged diversion of public resources By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has attributed the infrastructural and environmental challenges inherited by his administration to the alleged diversion of public resources by some politicians in the state. Otti said his administration had blocked entrenched channels through which public funds were allegedly siphoned, describing the former system as a political feeding bottle. The governor, who spoke at a two-day crusade organised by the Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Renewal Ministries at Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, said those criticising his administration were unhappy because they could no longer access public resources through the alleged channels. “Why they are murmuring is that we removed the feeding bottle from their mouths. And that feeding bottle was what they used to siphon all our resources. That was why there were no good roads and everywhere was dirty,” he said. Otti maintained that his administration would not reverse course despite criticisms, insisting that blocking access to public resources by vested interests was necessary to redirect government funds towards development. He cited road rehabilitation, improved environmental sanitation and drainage infrastructure in Aba as evidence of the changes recorded under his administration. According to him, the city has witnessed significant improvement in flood control, with floodwaters no longer lingering after heavy rainfall as they reportedly did in previous years. “Before now, there were no good roads, everywhere was dirty, the gutters were blocked, and whenever it rained, the entire place became flooded. “But I am sure that those of you living in Aba can testify that, despite the heavy rains this year, floodwaters no longer remain for long after the rains,” he said. He promised that the next four and a half years would focus on consolidating the gains already recorded. “What we have done in three and a half years is just the beginning of the rescue. The next four and a half years will be serious consolidation,” he declared. item.title: Okpe leaders demand restoration of distinct ethnic status in Delta
item.description: Leaders in Okpe Kingdom have urged their indigenous people to work towards restoring the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality, saying this would pave the way for the kingdom to regain its rightful status under the DESOPADEC Law, as was the case in the defunct Midwest Region and Bendel State. The elders, while reflecting on the historical position of the Okpe Union, said it would continue to push for the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality in Nigeria and Delta State. They made this known in a statement signed by Professor Igho Natufe, President-General, Okpe Union (Worldwide); Kingsley Akpederin, General Secretary, Okpe Union (Worldwide); and Victor Oruno, National Publicity Secretary, Okpe Union (Worldwide). The statement read: “Since the restoration of the Okpe Monarchy on January 1, 1945, after an interregnum of over 150 years, the Orodje institution has gradually re-established itself as one of the most important centres of administrative stability in Nigeria, contributing to the socio-economic and political evolution of the country and, most importantly, to inter-ethnic relations in the then Midwest Region (later known as Bendel State) and now Delta State. “At the creation of Delta State, the then Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhoro I, became the pioneer chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers. In furtherance of the legacy of the Okpe Nation as a rallying centre for the unity of the various ethnic nationalities in the Delta area, it is heartwarming that the Delta State Government recognised and appointed HRM Orhue I as Chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers. In this position, HRM Orhue I has contributed to the peaceful coexistence and security of our dear Delta State.” They also congratulated His Royal Majesty, Orhue I, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, and all Okpe nationals on the 20th anniversary of his coronation, being commemorated from November 13 to 22, 2026. The leaders praised the traditional ruler for his leadership and initiatives aimed at uplifting the people of Okpe Kingdom. “Back home in the Okpe Nation, there has been notable and sustained improvement in the infrastructural landscape of the Okpe Kingdom since 2006, when HRM Orhue I ascended the throne of the forefathers of the Okpe Nation. item.title: Plateau Council imposes curfew after gunmen burn seven houses
item.description: Residents flee Qua’an-Pan communities as tension mounts By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen set seven houses ablaze in Bong community. The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed amid reports of residents fleeing their homes, shops shutting down and commercial activities grinding to a halt over fears of further attacks. The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Cletus Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday, November 16, 2026. He said the curfew was necessary in view of the prevailing security situation in the district, warning that anyone found moving around during the restricted hours would be treated as a security threat by security agencies. The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace and prevent further breakdown of law and order. The development followed Sunday’s attack on Bong community in Doemak District, where suspected gunmen reportedly stormed the village at about 9pm and set seven houses on fire. A community source, Mr Silas Bishop, who confirmed the incident, lamented the destruction and called on security operatives to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible. He also urged security agencies to strengthen surveillance and deploy additional personnel to vulnerable communities to prevent further attacks. Meanwhile, tension has reportedly gripped Doemak, the headquarters of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area, with residents said to be packing their belongings and relocating to safer locations over fears for their lives and property. As of Monday evening, shops were reportedly closed, while commercial activities remained disrupted amid growing concerns over the security situation. Confirming the attack, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Hon. (Dr.) Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the incident and assured residents that the government would not abandon them. Manship, who visited Bong community to assess the destruction, pledged government support for efforts to rebuild the houses destroyed by the attackers. He said, “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks.” The chairman urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies. The attack on Bong occurred around the same time suspected terrorists invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several residents were reportedly killed. The rally, held at the Umuahia Township Stadium, attracted party leaders, candidates and supporters from across the state, with thousands of people filling the venue and causing heavy vehicular and human traffic around adjoining streets. According to him, the strategy could translate into more than 1.6 million votes for the President. “Don’t beg for 25 per cent. Your sons and daughters in Abia State will give you 75 per cent. We have about 2.3 million voters in Abia State. We are mobilising. We are not sleeping,” he declared. He said the party’s mobilisation efforts extended beyond rallies to house-to-house, village-to-village and community-to-community campaigns. The Deputy Speaker challenged those questioning the APC’s electoral strength in Abia to await the party’s proposed rally at Enyimba Stadium, Aba, on December 7, describing the Umuahia gathering, organised within one week, as a foretaste of what was to come. Kalu also appealed to Tinubu to reconsider his earlier decision to attend only the Enugu rally during his South-East campaign engagements and attend the proposed Aba rally. item.title: Oyebanji signs three laws, revises Ekiti ₦415.5bn budget
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI – Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has signed three new laws, including the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law, the Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law and the Right of Way Law. The laws were presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker of the State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Aribasoye, following their passage by the legislature. The 2026 Revised Appropriation Law retains the state’s total budget at ₦415.57 billion but adjusts the allocation between recurrent and capital expenditure. Under the revised budget, recurrent expenditure increases from ₦221.87 billion to ₦268.76 billion, while capital expenditure decreases from ₦193.69 billion to ₦146.80 billion. The adjustment represents a reallocation of funds from capital to recurrent expenditure to accommodate the state’s financial and operational obligations without increasing the overall budget approved in December 2025. The revised appropriation is expected to sustain government operations while maintaining funding for infrastructure, social development, economic growth and institutional efficiency. The second legislation, the Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026), amends the existing Pension Reform Law No. 3 of 2022 to formally accommodate the designation of a Director-General alongside the Permanent Secretary in the administrative and governance structure of the commission responsible for the Contributory Pension Scheme in the state. The amendment also makes consequential adjustments to relevant provisions of the principal law, including the composition of the commission’s board, staff administration, remuneration and allowances. The third legislation, the Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026 (No. 5 of 2026), establishes a regulatory framework for approving and administering permits for the installation and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure in the state. The law fixes the maximum Right of Way fee at ₦145 per linear metre for ducts and cables and ₦700,000 per site for a Base Transceiver Station. It also requires telecommunications operators to comply with approved engineering standards, protect public safety and the environment, minimise damage to roads and public utilities, and restore affected infrastructure after installation. The signing of the three laws underscores the Oyebanji administration’s efforts to strengthen public institutions, improve the regulatory environment for infrastructure development and ensure effective management of public resources. item.title: Count me out of Awka kingship, says Jeff Nweke
item.description: …Declares interest in governing Anambra State By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – Former governorship candidate of the Action Alliance (AA) in the last Anambra State governorship election, Ozo Jeff Nweke, has dismissed speculation that he is interested in becoming the next traditional ruler of Awka Kingdom, declaring that he has no ambition to occupy the throne. Nweke, a prominent indigene of Awka, said he was neither interested in becoming the traditional ruler nor a kingmaker, stressing that his political ambition was to govern Anambra State. Addressing reporters in Awka, he said aspiring to become the traditional ruler would not serve his political interests or his desire to contribute to the development of his people. He explained that speculations about his interest in the Eze Uzu Awka stool might have been fuelled by the construction of a large mansion, insisting that the size of his family informed the size of the property. “I want to make it clear that I am not interested in Awka kingship. Some people are insinuating that because I am building a mansion in a very large compound, that I am planning to become Eze Uzu Awka. This is not true. “I have a very large family. I am married to five wives and therefore someone who has up to 18 children should need a very large compound. It does not in any way mean that I am building a palace for Awka Kingdom,” he said. On the lingering crisis surrounding the Awka traditional institution, Nweke said the community was in an unusual situation with two individuals claiming the traditional stool. He identified the two as Eze Uzu II, whom he said was legitimately installed and recognised by the state government, and Eze Uzu III, who he said was also installed by the same kingmakers. “We have Eze Uzu II, who was legitimately installed as the traditional ruler of Awka Kingdom, and we also have Eze Uzu III. Eze Uzu II is there and nobody will take it away from him, especially as he is recognised by the state government. “Then we have Eze Uzu III, who was also legitimately installed by the same kingmakers who installed Eze Uzu II. However, since he is not recognised by government, what it means is that we have two kings in Awka,” he said. Nweke argued that if Eze Uzu II, being the older of the two, died, Eze Uzu III would assume the position, adding that speculation about his own succession to the throne was unfounded. He also pointed out that he came from the same village as the incumbent Eze Uzu II, saying there was no basis for him to aspire to succeed the traditional ruler. “My ambition is to become the gubernatorial candidate of my party in the next political dispensation. I am a politician and I want to do something for my people, and being a traditional ruler won’t serve that purpose,” he stated.
